question: A car covered 240 km in 5 h. If it travels with half of its usual speed, then how much more time will be taken to cover the same distance?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When Distance is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T).

Speed ratio (Original : New) = 1 : 1/2 = 2 : 1.

Time ratio (Original : New) = Inverse of speed ratio = 1 : 2.

Original time (1 unit) = 5 h.

More time taken = New time − Original time = 2 units − 1 unit = 1 unit.

Value of 1 unit = 5 h.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Distance = 240 km

Initial Time = 5 h

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/78b6030e8818b651ed1c6005f2d19484b263a0882aeb97ad6397cbfa618e52e2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Usual Speed = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 kmph

⇒ New Speed = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 kmph

⇒ New Time taken = 240 ÷ 24 = 10 h

⇒ Extra time = New Time − Initial Time

⇒ Extra time = 10 − 5 = 5 h

**∴ The correct answer is 5 h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is fixed, if the speed is multiplied by a factor n, the time is multiplied by 1/n.

Unit Conversion

To convert Speed from kmph to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to kmph, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a journey is divided into two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p
